title: Never using a hi-hat
summary: Watkins explains why he never bought a hi-hat and that earlier drummers such as Black Benny and Baby Dodds did not use one either.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Yeah. You never used tom cymbals?

No, I never used a hi-hat at no time. No, no. Because see in them days they never used hi-hats. No, no. And it's not necessary for, you use hi-hats and it gives a nice swing, I'll admit to that. It really gives a wonderful swing, but that's alright for these big bands, you understand what I mean? But for a small outfit like we got, we don't exactly need a hi-hat.
So you never used that at any time?
Because I get practically the same effect out of that one cymbal that I can get out of using a hi-hat. Yeah.
But you never used a hi-hat at any time?

No, not at any time. No, not at any time. Not no time, because I never did buy any. I had one outfit was given to me and I gave it away because it wasn't necessary that I'd use it because I wasn't accustomed to it. I'd have to start learning all over again with the hi-hat for one beat and the bass drum for one beat is more than one beat altogether with them two different outfits, you see?
So I get quite the same effect I get out of the one cymbal, you know?
Yeah, that's right. But say these other drummers, like Black Benny and that, they wouldn't have sock cymbals in those? No, they never used none either.
Baby Dots never used none either.
No. When was about the first time you saw a sock cymbal being used?
